svg.text: FRCS Part 1 (General Surgery) · NICE NG85 · presentation · resectability · pancreaticoduodenectomy · HPB (pancreas 1 of 3)
Painless obstructive jaundice + Courvoisier's law (palpable non-tender gallbladder); dark urine, pale stool, pruritus (60–70% of tumours)
Present late — epigastric pain radiating to the back, weight loss
New-onset diabetes; anorexia / cachexia; steatorrhoea; Trousseau's migratory thrombophlebitis
Smoking, chronic pancreatitis, obesity, diabetes; hereditary — BRCA2, PRSS1, Peutz–Jeghers, Lynch, FAMMM (CDKN2A)
Pancreatic-protocol dual-phase CT — diagnosis AND resectability staging
EUS ± FNA (small tumours, or tissue before chemo); not required before resection if imaging is typical & resectable
MRI / MRCP for indeterminate liver or biliary lesions; PET-CT for occult metastases
Adjunct & monitoring; falsely low if Lewis-antigen negative (~10%); raised by cholestasis / benign disease
matching the operation to the site
Head of pancreas, duodenum, distal CBD, gallbladder, proximal jejunum ± distal stomach
Distal pancreatectomy + splenectomy (vaccinate); total pancreatectomy for diffuse disease
Most COMMON (10–33%); prokinetics, NG / NJ feeding, supportive
ISGPS: biochemical leak / grade B / grade C; check drain amylase day 3
Percutaneous drainage; late exocrine & endocrine insufficiency
Borderline resectable → neoadjuvant chemotherapy (± chemoradiotherapy), often FOLFIRINOX, then re-stage
gemcitabine + capecitabine (ESPAC-4, NICE NG85); mFOLFIRINOX (PRODIGE-24; OS 54.4 vs 35 mo) for fit patients; start ≤12 weeks
FOLFIRINOX (PS 0–1) or gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel (MPACT); single-agent gemcitabine if frail
Endoscopic self-expanding metal biliary stent (ERCP); percutaneous (PTC) if ERCP fails
Duodenal stent or surgical gastrojejunostomy for gastric-outlet obstruction
Coeliac plexus neurolysis; WHO analgesic ladder
PERT (Creon) for ALL patients (NICE); dietitian / nutrition; VTE prophylaxis
Courvoisier's law: a palpable, non-tender gallbladder with painless jaundice makes gallstones unlikely — suspect malignant obstruction
Do not delay resection for a tissue diagnosis — if imaging is typical and the tumour is resectable, proceed to surgery; a negative biopsy does
Resectability is decided by vascular contact (SMA, coeliac axis, SMV / portal vein) on pancreatic-protocol CT, not by tumour size.
CA19-9 can be normal in Lewis-antigen-negative patients and is falsely raised by cholestasis — interpret it alongside imaging.
Delayed gastric emptying is the commonest complication after a Whipple; a pancreatic fistula is the most dangerous — watch the drain
amylase and for a sentinel bleed.
Offer pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT) to all patients with pancreatic cancer (NICE NG85).
Sources: NICE NG85 (pancreatic cancer in adults, 2018) · resectability per NCCN vascular criteria · ISGPS definitions (POPF, DGE, post-pancreatectomy haemorrhage). Adjuvant: ESPAC-4
(gemcitabine + capecitabine); PRODIGE-24 (adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX). Metastatic: PRODIGE/ACCORD-11 (FOLFIRINOX); MPACT (gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel).
Pancreatic cystic neoplasms and neuroendocrine tumours are on the companion sheets (pancreas 2 & 3 of 3).
